references.text: The Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth below—a parallel confession of God's sovereignty over heaven and earth.
The nations heard about Israel's exodus from Egypt and were seized with fear; their hearts melted—the same reaction Rahab describes.
God promises to send fear ahead of Israel so that enemies lose courage—fulfillment of this promise.
The hearts of the Amorite kings and Canaanite kings melted when they heard about the Lord's deeds—the same reaction Rahab described.
Israel's hearts melted after the defeat at Ai—the same expression used for Israel itself.
Solomon's prayer confesses that the Lord is God in heaven above and on the earth below—the same theological confession.
Our God is in heaven; he does whatever he pleases—a confession of God's sovereign rule.
All hands grow limp, and every human heart melts—the same image of fear and discouragement.
Christ as head over all things in heaven and on earth—continuation of the confession of God's sovereignty.
